nodes.label: Threat Model, Honestly Stated
nodes.rationale: An LLM with file access reads untrusted web content (job postings) alongside personal data (CV, profile, application history). That combination is the main risk surface and cannot be eliminated, only narrowed - instruction-level defenses raise the bar but are not a sandbox.

nodes.label: Untrusted-Input Rules for Postings
nodes.rationale: /apply and /rank treat posting text as data, never instructions, and fetch no URLs found inside posting bodies (the user-supplied posting URL being the sole exception). Reviewer research starts from the company identity the user confirmed.

nodes.label: Claude Code Permission Allowlist
nodes.rationale: .claude/settings.json pre-approves only the commands the workflow needs. Stated limit: the allowlist governs Bash commands only - the model's native WebFetch/WebSearch are outside its reach, which is precisely why the instruction-level untrusted-input rules exist.

nodes.label: Personal Data Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Populated profile, tracker, salary data and application archive are gitignored; documents never leave the machine by design - /notion-sync syncs filenames only and nothing uploads document content anywhere.

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting Policy
nodes.rationale: Private GitHub advisory reporting keeps a working recipe out of public view until a patch exists; if the private form is unavailable, describe the class of problem without the recipe. Community fork skills are explicitly out of scope.

hyperedges.label: Layered defenses for untrusted job-posting content
